You are judging a candidate's attempt to reproduce a research paper.

You will first be given the research paper, which you should read carefully and refer to as the ground truth for what constitutes a correct implementation and reproduction.

Following that, you will be presented with the candidate's submission: a set of files that attempts
to reproduce the paper. The candidate has been asked to include a `reproduce.sh` script that, when executed, should run the full reproduction process and generate all results in the paper. If the script exists, we have already run it and included any output logs in the file `reproduce.log`. Any other files generated by the script may also be present, such as results, plots, or artifacts. If either `reproduce.sh` or `reproduce.log` is missing, you should consider any criteria relying on it to have failed.

To judge the submission, we have prepared a full rubric describing fine-grained criteria for different aspects of the paper.

Your task is to check the submission and its outputs for ONE specific criterion from this rubric.

The paper is below:
version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1
oid sha256:4dc3ecabd26f0dce90405a010f194a192089980dd504ccb928e22c03344a7bf9
size 108821

If included with the paper, you will now be shown an addendum which provides clarification for the paper and how to evaluate its reproduction:
<addendum>

oid sha256:ebe0d30d2364caa20ddaaf4f0322eb1fa5639df21eb845bfcd86db4e3b5ba90b
size 6659
</addendum>

<files>

<reproduce.sh>

</reproduce.sh>

<reproduce.log>
(Does not exist)
</reproduce.log>

The full grading rubric for the paper hierarchically decomposes various aspects of the paper. To provide more context for the criterion you are currently grading, here are some of the preceding criteria (DO NOT grade this, this is just for context):
<preceding_criteria>
 -> The paper "All-in-one simulation-based inference" has been reproduced.
 -> Variance Exploding SDE (VESDE) is implemented, as described in A2.1
 -> The Simformer model, training process and inference process has been implemented
 -> Baseline methods Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE), Neural Ratio Estimation (NRE), and Neural Likelihood Estimation (NLE) are implemented
 -> The benchmark tasks are prepared
 -> The recorded metrics show that the results from section 4 are replicated
 -> The hyperparameters for Simformer stated in Section A.2.1 are used in all experiments, unless otherwise stated
 -> Variance Exploding SDE (VESDE) is used to train the Simformer in all experiments
 -> The recorded metrics show that the results in section 4.1 have been replicated
 -> Simformers used for all experiments in Section 4.1 have 6 layers
 -> The experiments in 4.1 related to approximating the posterior distribution have been replicated
 -> The experiments in 4.1 related to evaluating arbitrary conditionals have been replicated
 -> For the Tree and HMM tasks, each of the following models have been trained for 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 simulations (in separate training runs): 1) Simformer (with a dense attention mask), 2) Simformer with an undirected graph for it's attention mask, 3) Simformer with a directed graph for it's attention mask
 -> For the Tree task, each of the following models have been trained for 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 simulations (in separate training runs): 1) Simformer (with a dense attention mask), 2) Simformer with an undirected graph for it's attention mask, 3) Simformer with a directed graph for it's attention mask
 -> For the HMM task, each of the following models have been trained for 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 simulations (in separate training runs): 1) Simformer (with a dense attention mask), 2) Simformer with an undirected graph for it's attention mask, 3) Simformer with a directed graph for it's attention mask
 -> For the HMM task, Simformer (with a dense attention mask) has been trained for 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 simulations (in separate training runs)
 -> For the HMM task, Simformer (with an undirected graph for it's attention mask) has been trained for 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 simulations (in separate training runs)

</preceding_criteria>

Now, here is the criterion that you are grading:
<criterion>
For the HMM task, Simformer (with a directed graph for it's attention mask) has been trained for 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 simulations (in separate training runs)
</criterion>

The criterion you are grading is of type Code Execution - Does running the reproduce.sh script lead to this being successfully executed?

You will now evaluate the submission above for the given criterion.

Please present your answer in 3 parts as follows:

# Expectations
Read the paper carefully to identify the parts relevant to your criterion. Describe what you expect correct resolution to look like, and what you will specifically look for in the submission.

# Reality
Explore the files provided for the submission along with the output logs to identify the parts that are relevant to the resolution criteria. When you have identified the relevant parts, comment on how they compare to your expectations above, and whether the attempt meets the resolution criteria. Be sure to describe only what has been given to you in the submission, and be explicit about which files you are referring to when you discuss them.

# Score
Reason about whether the criteria has been met. Give a score of either 0 or 1 depending on whether the criteria has been met, and explain why.

Other notes:
- You must always provide a score. If you have any uncertainties, make them clear in your discussion.
- All the files and logs from the submission attempt have been provided to you. If anything appears to be missing, assume that the attempt failed to produce it (treat it as a failure).
- Be strict and thorough in grading your resolution criteria, but do not check for things that are outside of your scope.

# Expectations
The criterion requires that for the HMM task, the Simformer model with a directed graph for its attention mask is trained across three separate runs, specifically for 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 simulations. In order to meet this criterion, I would expect to find a clear indication of this training process in the implementation provided by the candidate. I would look for the following in the submission:

1. Evidence of the HMM task being executed, specifically using the Simformer model.
2. Confirmation that the training runs are executed specifically with the directed graph attention mask.
3. Logs or outputs that show the execution of these specific training runs for the specified number of simulations (10^3, 10^4, and 10^5).

I would anticipate finding these details in the `reproduce.sh` script or any generated log files such as `reproduce.log`. If these files are missing, I would interpret that as not fulfilling the criteria.

# Reality
Upon reviewing the submission, it is clear that the `reproduce.sh` script does not exist, nor does the `reproduce.log`. Without these files, there is no documentation or script to examine that could demonstrate the training of the Simformer model on the HMM task with the directed graph attention mask over the specified number of simulations. 

The absence of the script indicates that the execution process for the reproduction has not been completed, and subsequently, I cannot evaluate whether the criterion has been met based on any output or results. Without any further materials to indicate successful completion of the training runs needed for the HMM task, it is impossible to assert that the criterion has been satisfied.

# Score
The score for this criterion is 0. The absence of both `reproduce.sh` and `reproduce.log` means there is no way to validate that the Simformer model was trained for the HMM task with a directed graph attention mask across the required number of simulations. Thus, the condition set forth in the criterion has not been met.
